'''Ian Thomas Baldwin''' (born 1958) is an American ecologist.

==Early life==
Baldwin's parents were the medieval historians [[Jenny Jochens]] and [[John W. Baldwin]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=McCormick |first=Michael |title=John W. Baldwin, 13 July 1929. 8 February 2015 |url=https://www.amphilsoc.org/sites/default/files/2017-07/attachments/Baldwin.pdf |journal=Proceedings of the American Philosophical Society |volume=160 |issue=4 |pages=450-55}}</ref>{{Reference page|page=450}}

== Scientific career ==
Baldwin studied biology and chemistry at [[Dartmouth College]] in Hanover, New Hampshire, and graduated 1981 with an AB. In 1989 he graduated with a PhD in [[chemical ecology]] from [[Cornell University]], Ithaca, New York, Section of Neurobiology and Behavior. He was an Assistant (1989), Associate (1993) and Full Professor (1996) in the Department of Biology at [[University at Buffalo, The State University of New York|SUNY Buffalo]]. In 1996 he became the Founding Director of the [[Max Planck Institute for Chemical Ecology]] where he heads the Department of Molecular Ecology.<ref>[https://ice.mpg.de MPI for Chemical Ecology Website]. Retrieved on October 8, 2013.</ref> In 1999 he was appointed Honorary Professor at [[Friedrich Schiller University]] in Jena, Germany. In 2002 he founded the International Max Planck Research School at the Max Planck Institute in Jena.<ref>[http://imprs.ice.mpg.de/ext/ ''The Exploration of Ecological Interactions with Molecular and Chemical Techniques'']- IMPRS Home Page</ref>

Baldwin's scientific work is devoted to understanding the traits that allow plants to survive in the real world. To achieve this, he has developed a molecular toolbox for the native tobacco, ''[[Nicotiana attenuata]]'' (coyote tobacco),<ref>[https://discovermagazine.com/2002/apr/featplants ''Talking Plants''] Discover Magazine, April 1, 2002</ref><ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1038/468886a|title=Plant biology: Growth industry|year=2010|last1=Abbott|first1=Alison|journal=Nature|volume=468|issue=7326|pages=886–8|pmid=21164459 |bibcode=2010Natur.468..886A|doi-access=free}}</ref> and a graduate program that trains "genome-enabled field biologists" to combine genomic and molecular genetic tools with field work to understand the genes that matter for plant-herbivore, -pollinator, -plant, -microbial interactions in nature.<ref>[http://www.mpg.de/15791/Plants_and_environment ''Interaction of plants with their environment'']{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} Research Perspectives 2010+ of the Max Planck Society</ref> He has been a driver behind the [[Open Access]] publication efforts of the [[Max Planck Society]] and is one of the senior editors of the [[open access journal]] [[eLife]].<ref>[https://www.mpg.de/4634182/elife ''Editorial team announced for 'eLife', the new open access journal to be launched next year'']. MPG News. November 7, 2011</ref><ref>[http://elifesciences.org/about ''Pain-free publishing for your best science'']. eLife Journal Homepage</ref> 
Since  November 2020, the Department of Molecular Ecology is led by Acting Director [[Sarah O’Connor]].  The former Director Ian Baldwin now serves as Leader of the Research Group of a Scientific Member of the Max Planck Society (FG WiMi, Forschungsgruppe Wissenschaftliches Mitglied) and he continues his research at the Institute in this role. <ref>MPI-CE. Change of Leadership of the Department of Molecular Ecology [https://www.ice.mpg.de/ext/index.php?id=1671].</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
* Presidential Young Investigator Award 1991
* Silverstein-Simeone Award of the [https://www.chemecol.org International Society of Chemical Ecology] 1998<ref>[https://www.chemecol.org/ ISCE Home Page]. Chemecol.org. Retrieved on October 8, 2013.</ref>
* Extraordinary member of the [[Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities]] (since 2001)
* Tansley Lecture, [[British Ecological Society]], 2009<ref>[http://www.britishecologicalsociety.org/meetings/annual_meetings_archive/2009_annual_meeting/bes_tansley_lectures.php ''Using Transformed Native Plants to Study Ecological Interactions''] {{webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20120722051730/http://www.britishecologicalsociety.org/meetings/annual_meetings_archive/2009_annual_meeting/bes_tansley_lectures.php |date=July 22, 2012 }} Tansley Lecture 2009</ref>
* [[European Research Council]] (ERC) Advanced Grant 2011<ref>[https://www.mpg.de/5004106/erc_grants_2012_en ''Max Planck scientists very pleased about ERC grants'']. MPG News. January 30, 2012</ref>
* Elected Member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] 2013 <ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20130501022503/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2013_04_30_NAS_Election.html ''National Academy of Sciences Members and Foreign Associates Elected''] News from the National Academy of Sciences, April 30, 2013</ref>
* Elected Member of the [[German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]] 2013 <ref>[http://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2013-09/mpif-poe090613.php "Pioneer of ecological genetics"] News Release, EurekAlert, September 6, 2013</ref>
* Elected Member of the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] EMBO <ref>[https://www.embo.org/news/press-releases/press-releases-2014/embo-enlarges-its-membership-for-50th-anniversary ''EMBO enlarges its membership for 50th anniversary''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160307070519/http://embo.org/news/press-releases/press-releases-2014/embo-enlarges-its-membership-for-50th-anniversary |date=March 7, 2016 }} EMBO Press Release, May 7, 2014</ref>
* International Award of the Jean-Marie Delwart Foundation 2014<ref>[http://www.fondationjeanmariedelwart.org/index.php?lang=en Website of the Fondation Jean-Marie Delwart]</ref>
* Elected Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] 2016<ref>[https://www.aaas.org/2016-fellows AAAS proudly congratulates the newly elected 2016 Fellows!]</ref>
